chapter: Billie Holiday, Art Tatum and Chicago hotels
title: Billie Holiday and 'Lady Sings the Blues'; his band at the Three Deuces
summary: Prompted by the Diana Ross film, he recalls his own band at the Three Deuces with Anita O'Day, Billie Holiday as star and Art Tatum playing intermission.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Although we've talked about a lot of things, I still have bits and pieces of our conversation, earlier conversation in my mind. And I'd like to go back to Chicago for just a moment because I think you said there you used to go and hear Billie Holiday? Used to work with Billie Holiday?
And if it's any time to talk about her it's now with the play 'Lady Day' (Betty Davis) which I saw. And by the way, Archie Shepp spent at least four days working on his music at this very piano.
Yes. He did. He was staying in the hotel then and of course the film is sensational.
I saw the film and Diana Ross did to me one of the greatest bits of acting.

She did one of the greatest bits of acting that I have ever seen on the screen. Because firstly I knew Billie very well. I had known her, but we worked together. As a matter of fact, well let's see, it was after I left the Pollack band. I got back to Chicago and I formed my own band and I went

to 'The Three Deuces' I think it was. And Anita O'Day was my girl singer. And I had some fine musicians. An excellent band, all fine jazz musicians. A good arranger and Floyd Bean on the piano. And I was the MC of the deal and Billie Holiday was our star singing. And by the way, Art Tatum was playing the intermission piano.
